reviews.title: Life changing

After starting calm, I quickly found 7 days to better sleep, which got me thinking about my sleep differently. I started meditating during the day, using breathing techniques or sleep stories at night, and over time I did become a better- dare I say good- sleeper. My anxiety during the day decreased and I am more content than I have ever been now that I sleep better. Thanks, calm!

reviews.title: Excellent resource; some mediocre features
reviews.text: The variety and value of each practice and session really make this my go-to app for mental self-care; I’ve been using it for years to get through a variety of challenging times. I wish there were more shorter, practice-only follow-up / maintenance sessions without as much explanation in the themed meditation series. For example, I’d love shorter sessions from Lama Rod, Elisha Goldstein, or Tara Brach that are like quick reminder or check-in sessions touching on the practices and focus of their existing series. Also, the customization has gotten less-helpful and user-friendly recently; my favorites and recents don’t seem accurate, so I find I constantly have to type in a search to find something I just accessed a day ago. The bi-lateral EMDR-inspired playlists are really helpful, but half the time they don’t auto play or shuffle, stopping after 1-2 tracks.

reviews.title: Truly a life saver
reviews.text:
I’ve been using the Calm app for about six years, and it has truly become one of my go-to tools.

My struggle with anxiety and overthinking is real. There are times when my mind simply does not want to slow down, and Calm has consistently given me a place to reset, breathe, refocus, and find a little peace.

Whether I need help quieting my thoughts, relaxing, sleeping, or just taking a few intentional minutes for myself, I know I can open the app and find something that meets me where I am.

I recommend Calm all the time and have shared it with so many people over the years because I genuinely use it and believe in it. Six years later, I’m still here—and that says a lot.

If you struggle with anxiety, overthinking, stress, or simply need a tool that reminds you to slow down and be present, Calm is absolutely worth trying.

reviews.title: Long-time subscriber lost because support simply doesn’t exist
reviews.text:
I was a long-time paying subscriber, and I finally cancelled.

The app stopped working properly for me, leaving me unable to reliably use a service I was paying a premium subscription price for. I contacted support for help.

They responded more than a month later.

By then, I had already cancelled my subscription because I refuse to continue paying for an app I cannot use while waiting weeks for someone to acknowledge the problem.

Technical issues happen. That isn’t why I’m leaving this review. I’m leaving it because a company charging this much for a subscription should provide a reasonable level of support when its paying customers cannot access the product they purchased.

What is particularly disappointing is that I actually liked the service. I subscribed for a long time. I wasn’t looking for a reason to cancel—I wanted someone to help me continue using something I was already happily paying for.

Instead, they turned a loyal subscriber into a former customer.

If you’re considering subscribing, understand that the price gets you access to the app when it works. Based on my experience, it does not get you timely help when it doesn’t.

A month-plus response time isn’t customer support. It’s an autopsy of a customer relationship that already died waiting.

reviews.title: Why did you ruin a once amazing app?
reviews.text:
Sometime recently, there was an upgrade, which I never worry about doing, and it seemed to ruin the entire app. I understand, sometimes things change and it used to this is just been infuriating, and I am about to delete something that I have been using almost daily for many years.
The biggest problem is that the multiple chapter stories and the song collections with multiple songs have gotten ruined. Some of my favorite multi Chapter stories now just go to one chapter somewhere, but it doesn’t even tell you where you are so a five parts story that I last episode number five now only shows me episode five like there’s never been anything else. Why would you??
Also song collections that I used to put on a two hour timer and go to sleep to some amazingly, beautiful and relaxing music, has one son associated with each like harp, music, or cello music, it’s no longer a collection of music for the Harper the cello song playing on a harp or a cello. And make it worse, when you set a two hour timer it just repeats that one song over and over for two hours. Absolutely disgusting, absolutely infuriating, and how could you let anyone ruin an app like this? I’ll check back in about a week and if it has not been resolved, then all my, I think four years? Maybe more, of enjoyment of an app that I really enjoy having Has just because somebody decided to do an update and obviously hasn’t paid any attention they broke in the process.
I cannot convey my discussed, anger, or frustration, enough in words!!!

reviews.title: The difference calm has made
reviews.text:
I’ve been doing the daily meditations for a couple years. Occasionally, I miss a day, but I have developed a 15 minute routine where I sit outside in the early morning quiet, and listen to meditations with Tamara and Jeff and Jay. Sometimes I listen to just one, other times I have time for all three and every time I take something away. 

 I’ve noticed how I can hold onto Calm and steadiness throughout the rest of my day. I also have noticed when handling stressful situations lately, I tend to not react and get as overwhelmed, and I think this is the benefit of practicing daily centering meditations. I use the sleep stories and the sleep meditations, the daily meditations, and the soundscapes. And I recommend calm as often as I can!
